clue.text: Close to four, old boy elected to prepare vestry

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the final letter of four is wanted

parts.note: last letter of four
OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a party that is elected is IN power
to groom is to prepare or make ready

explanation.surface: Just before four o'clock, a former pupil voted in is told to get the church vestry ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A robing room is where clergy put on their vestments, which is exactly what a vestry is used for.

clue.text: Excellent artist, extremely reasonable

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of reasonable

explanation.surface: Praise for a painter who is highly sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare can mean unusually good, as in 'a rare treat' or 'we had a rare time'.

clue.text: Invoice committee for hoarding

parts.note: a bill is an invoice
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A bill sent to a committee for some fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoarding is the British word for a large outdoor panel bearing advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: A billboard is a large outdoor board for posters, which the British also call a hoarding.

clue.text: Top technician prepared something for an addict?

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, here from reworked letters

explanation.surface: A leading technician has made up something to help someone hooked on a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: A nicotine patch is stuck to the skin to help a smoker quit; the question mark admits the addict is a smoker.

clue.text: Normal uniform

explanation.definitionFit: Regular means both ordinary and evenly spaced or consistent.

clue.text: Supervise across diocese

parts.note: over means across, as in 'over the road'
a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A bishop is asked to supervise matters throughout the diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to watch over and direct work, the same as to supervise.

clue.text: Benefit of luxurious hotel overlooked

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so the hotel letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: plush means luxurious
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A guest remarks that a perk of a posh hotel went unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or good point, the same as a benefit.

clue.text: Left sheep in East Sussex location

parts.note: ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: Some sheep have been abandoned somewhere in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex in southern England.

clue.text: Closely examine small vessel during holiday at sea

parts.note: S is the clothing abbreviation for small

indicators.note: during puts the vessel inside the holiday

parts.note: a cruise is a holiday on a ship
a tin is a container, a vessel

explanation.surface: Inspect a little boat while on a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship to go with the cruise, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise is to inspect something carefully and in detail.

clue.text: Historical object held by derelict

indicators.note: held by says the answer is kept inside the next word's letters

parts.note: the letters sit within derelict

explanation.surface: An old artefact is found in the possession of a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from the past, often of historical interest.

clue.text: Welsh chieftain's scowl accepting death

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to glower is to scowl
end can mean death, as in 'came to a sticky end'

explanation.surface: A Welsh leader frowns as he faces up to dying.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay. Owain Glyndwr, anglicised as Owen Glendower, led a Welsh revolt against English rule around 1400.
explanation.definitionFit: Glendower was the medieval Welsh prince who led a rebellion, so a chieftain of Wales.

clue.text: Relative's hurting a lad, we suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: We think a relation is hurting a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter-in-law is a son's wife, a relation by marriage.

clue.text: Campaigns of British PM almost succeeded

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the name is cut

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister after the Second World War
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: A political history of a British prime minister who nearly made it.
explanation.definitionFit: Battles and campaigns are both military operations; the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Winning group's surprise result

parts.note: a team that is ahead is UP
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A sports report says a winning team produced an unexpected result.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an upset is a shock win by the underdog, an unexpected outcome.

clue.text: Hope to have most of jelly with helping

indicators.note: most of means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: aspic is a savoury jelly
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to get the larger share of a jelly with their serving.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is an ambition or longing, a hope for the future.

clue.text: Tool — second one missing from saddlebag

indicators.note: missing from means the named letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a pannier is a bag hung either side of a bike or horse
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A cyclist finds a tool has gone missing from a bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanner is a hand tool for turning nuts and bolts; Americans call it a wrench.

clue.text: Copy includes the Spanish name and rank

indicators.note: includes means the first word holds the next inside it

parts.note: to echo is to copy or repeat
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a duplicate including the Spanish name and rank of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a level or grade in an organisation, so a rank.

clue.text: Girl touring island, an American state

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the girl's name surrounds the island letter

parts.note: Louisa is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl on a trip around an island, an American who sees the states.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is a state in the southern US, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Detailed batting strength

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a cricket team with good batsmen far down the order has batting ...

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting order runs to eleven; a side whose lower-order players can also score well is said to bat in depth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes thorough treatment of a subject and also the reserves of a cricket line-up.

clue.text: Type of car difficult to park, at first

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of park

parts.note: first letter of park

explanation.surface: A kind of car that is tricky to park at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid roof, often a detachable one on a convertible.

clue.text: Sweet children with her, surrounded by cheeky young boys?

indicators.note: surrounded by means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a cub is an impudent young lad, and Cubs are junior Scouts

explanation.surface: Adorable children are with a girl, ringed by impudent little boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubs are winged infant angels in art, so the word is used for lovely, innocent-looking children.

clue.text: London initially in dispute with Reykjavik leads to an international conflict

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the dispute

parts.note: the Cod Wars were fishing disputes between Britain and Iceland, whose capital is Reykjavik

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of London

parts.note: first letter of London

explanation.surface: A London quarrel with Iceland escalates into conflict between nations.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Cod Wars of the 1950s-70s Britain and Iceland clashed over fishing limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cold War was the long post-1945 standoff between the US and Soviet blocs, a conflict between nations.

clue.text: Sailor away, here and there

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor
out means away, not at home

explanation.surface: A sailor is away at sea, roaming here and there.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving about means scattered or going in various directions, as in 'wander about'.

clue.text: It may bring tears to your eyes about India (cricket side)

definitions.text: It may bring tears to your eyes

parts.note: on means about, as in 'a book on birds'
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Something about Indian cricket that might make you cry.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping an onion releases a compound that makes the eyes water.

clue.text: Picks up supporters by end of pier

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of pier
allies are supporters

explanation.surface: Someone collects backers at the far end of a seaside pier.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up is to recover, as a market or patient rallies after a fall.

clue.text: Loud, a church clock

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church clock described as loud.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'church clock' together, but 'clock' alone is the definition, a slang noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a person's clock is their face, as in 'look at his clock'.

clue.text: Tries his cooking before wife produces a traditional dish

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being worked into something new

explanation.surface: A man tries his hand in the kitchen before his wife serves a classic meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges TRIES HIS into IRISHST; 'before' places that ahead of W.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish stew is a long-established stew of mutton, potatoes and onions from Ireland.

clue.text: Monk after large pack animal

indicators.note: after says the monk comes behind the large letter

parts.note: L is the clothing abbreviation for large
a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk

explanation.surface: A monk follows a large beast of burden along a mountain path.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelids used for carrying loads in the Andes.

clue.text: Number taking part in Pygmalion, in earnest

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cast member appearing in Shaw's Pygmalion, played seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: Pygmalion is George Bernard Shaw's play; the surface pretends a performer is acting in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is a numeral, one of the counting numbers.

clue.text: Helper swam out to see sea creature

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A helper swims out to look at a creature in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The sperm whale is a large toothed whale, a marine mammal.
